Kaluszyn Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kałuszyn, Poland

Demolished. Jews are confirmed in Kałuszyn from the second half of the 18th century; in 1849, Tzadik Awraham Elchanan Unger founded a local Hasidic dynasty continued by Awi Ezra Zelig Unger and Jaakow Icchak Unger, while rabbis Uri Jehoszua, Asher Elchanan, Aszkenazy Rabinowicz, and Meir Rabinowicz were also linked to the town. By 1921, 5,033 (82%) were mostly killed by Germans in 1942; postwar survivors faced further murders in the area. This original cemetery, probably established in the 18th century, was fenced in 1829 and enclosed with stone and concrete by the early 20th century; Germans repurposed tombstones for construction and tore down the wall during WWII. Poland formally closed the cemetery on October 9, 1964, describing it as 'closed for about 60 years and completely devastated (there are no traces).' The town's current City Hall was later built on the grounds.
